title: Implement LRU cache eviction
statement:
Step 3 · Caching and admission

An LRU cache evicts the least recently accessed key. Reads and updates refresh recency; misses do not. This local cache has no TTL, concurrency, replication, or persistence.

Build it

Simulate put(key,value) and get(key) operations. Return one result per get, using None for misses. capacity is a nonnegative integer; values are integers. Do not mutate operations.

Contract: Implement lru using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: capacity = 2, operations = [["put", "a", 1], ["put", "b", 2], ["get", "a"], ["put", "c", 3], ["get", "b"], ["get", "c"]]
Expected: [1, null, 3]
Input: capacity = 0, operations = [["put", "x", 7], ["get", "x"]]
Expected: [null]
Hint

OrderedDict supports moving a key to the newest end and removing the oldest item.

Review your understanding

What happens with a hot key, stale values, a cache stampede, or a process restart?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
